fields.meta_title: Travel Quiz Builder: Play One, Then Make Yours | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Take an 8-question travel quiz that matches you to a city break, beach, mountain, or road trip, then build one for an agency, tour, or hotel.
fields.h1: Build a Travel Quiz for Agencies, Tours, and Hotels
fields.hero_description: Build a travel quiz that matches each traveler to a trip and saves every result, or take the 8-question one below.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Travel Quiz
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the quiz and the table behind it from one prompt, and a second prompt changes either one before the next season.
fields.feature_1:
Every option points to one trip

Name the trips you sell as results. Emergent writes questions about pace and budget, with each option pointing to one result, and a follow-up prompt rewrites any question.
fields.feature_2:
Result screens that list real tours

Tag each tour or package with one result. The result screen lists the trips carrying that tag, read from your booking system through its API, and retagging a tour updates the quiz.
fields.feature_3:
An advisor alert for each new lead

When a taker leaves an email, the app sends the assigned advisor a Slack or email message with the result and budget. The advisor opens the first call knowing which trip to pitch.
fields.feature_4:
Every finish saved as a database row

Each finish is a row in a database you own, holding the result, every answer, and the email. A live dashboard counts results by month for planning next year's departure dates.
fields.feature_5:
One question per screen on a phone

Travelers answer one question per screen with a progress bar, at a gate or on a lunch break. Emergent puts no cap on responses, and the busiest August still saves every finish.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain and your code

Run the quiz on a custom domain, included in Emergent and paid for with credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep each season's quiz in history.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Travel Businesses Running a Quiz
fields.tab_content_1:
With a Beach Escape result, Tadeusz calls the same day

Kirsikka Ferreira-Nunes finds the travel quiz on Ebbtide Travel's site and finishes on Beach Escape, with a budget under $4,000. Her answers and email save to the leads table. Advisor Tadeusz Gwilliam gets a Slack message with her result and calls her the same day.
fields.tab_content_2:
In March, Mountain Trip led with 212 of 640

Each result at Tamsarra Tours points to one tour style. Owner Haukur Ulloa opens the March dashboard and finds 640 finished quizzes, with Mountain Trip at 212 and Beach Escape next at 171. He adds a third departure date for the alpine hiking tour.
fields.tab_content_3:
Three walking tours for each City Break guest

Seven days before arrival, Cindral House emails every guest the quiz. Zofia Quorrin answers on her phone and lands on City Break, and her welcome note lists 3 walking tours near the hotel. Concierge Emrys Vasquez-Lind books all 3 before she checks in.
fields.tab_content_4:
Eight of 10 correct before an agent takes calls

New agents at Brackenmoor Travel Group take a 10-question destination quiz with a pass mark of 8, scored against an answer key. Agents at the pass mark start on client calls. Basilio Ystad scores 9 of 10, and his row in the training table flips to cleared.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a travel quiz?

quiz_plan.promise: the quiz plays the page's promise: a travel quiz a visitor can take, whose results answer what the H1 says it builds

plan.angle: The top 10 splits into destination pickers from travel brands and publishers and lists of travel trivia questions; only one builder ranks, and none shows a quiz feeding a business. This page lets a visitor play an 8-question travel quiz that matches them to a City Break, Beach Escape, Mountain Trip, or Road Trip, then shows four travel businesses using results: an agency routes a result to an advisor, a tour operator counts results by month to plan departures, a hotel turns a pre-arrival result into a welcome note, and an agency group scores new agents on a 10-question knowledge quiz. Every result lands in a database the owner keeps. The FAQ covers question writing, answer keys, result count, length, lead capture, tour picks, and reading results.
tab_stories: Kirsikka Ferreira-Nunes takes the travel quiz on Ebbtide Travel's site, lands on Beach Escape with a budget under $4,000, and advisor Tadeusz Gwilliam gets a Slack message with her result while her answers and email save to the leads table.

Tamsarra Tours maps each of the 4 results to one tour style, and owner Haukur Ulloa sees 640 finished quizzes in March with Mountain Trip leading at 212, so he adds a third departure date for the alpine hiking tour.

Cindral House emails the quiz to guests 7 days before arrival, Zofia Quorrin's City Break result puts 3 walking tours in her welcome note, and concierge Emrys Vasquez-Lind books them before she lands.
Brackenmoor Travel Group gives each new agent a 10-question knowledge quiz with a pass mark of 8, and Basilio Ystad scores 9 of 10 and is cleared to take client calls.
